# Verify a smart contract on Monad using Foundry

Once your contract is deployed to a live network, the next step is to verify its source code on the block explorer.

Verifying a contract means uploading its source code, along with the settings used to compile the code, to a
repository (typically maintained by a block explorer). This allows anyone to compile it and compare the generated
bytecode with what is deployed on chain. Doing this is extremely important in an open platform like Monad.

In this guide we'll explain how to do this using [Foundry](/tooling-and-infra/toolkits/foundry.md) v1.8 or later with the Monad execution environment enabled.

> [!TIP]
>
> This guide assumes you have Foundry v1.8.0 or later installed and `network = "monad"` configured in `foundry.toml`. See the [installation and configuration instructions](/tooling-and-infra/toolkits/foundry.md#installation) if you haven't set it up yet.

**Mainnet**

**Foundry Monad template (Recommended)**

> [!NOTE]
>
> The [`foundry-monad`](https://github.com/monad-developers/foundry-monad) template is configured for testnet by default. To use mainnet, update your `foundry.toml` file:
>
> * Change `eth-rpc-url="https://testnet-rpc.monad.xyz"` to your mainnet RPC URL
> * Change `chain_id = 10143` to `143`

If you are using [`foundry-monad`](https://github.com/monad-developers/foundry-monad) template, you can use the commands below based on your preferred block explorer:

**MonadVision**

```sh theme={null}
forge verify-contract \
    <contract_address> \
    <contract_name> \
    --chain 143 \
    --verifier sourcify \
    --verifier-url https://sourcify-api-monad.blockvision.org/
```

**Example:**

```sh theme={null}
forge verify-contract \
    0x8fEc29BdEd7A618ab6E3CD945456A79163995769 \
    Counter \
    --chain 143 \
    --verifier sourcify \
    --verifier-url https://sourcify-api-monad.blockvision.org/
```

On successful verification of smart contract, you should get a similar output in your terminal:

```sh theme={null}
Start verifying contract `0x8fEc29BdEd7A618ab6E3CD945456A79163995769` deployed on monad-mainnet
Attempting to verify on Sourcify. Pass the --etherscan-api-key <API_KEY> to verify on Etherscan, or use the --verifier flag to verify on another provider.

Submitting verification for [Counter] "0x8fEc29BdEd7A618ab6E3CD945456A79163995769".
Contract successfully verified
```

Now check the contract on MonadVision.

**Monadscan**

```sh theme={null}
forge verify-contract \
    <contract_address> \
    <contract_name> \
    --chain 143 \
    --verifier etherscan \
    --etherscan-api-key YourApiKeyToken \
    --watch
```

**Example:**

```sh theme={null}
forge verify-contract \
    0x8fEc29BdEd7A618ab6E3CD945456A79163995769 \
    Counter \
    --chain 143 \
    --verifier etherscan \
    --etherscan-api-key YourApiKeyToken \
    --watch
```

On successful verification of smart contract, you should get a similar output in your terminal:

```sh theme={null}
Start verifying contract `0x8fEc29BdEd7A618ab6E3CD945456A79163995769` deployed on monad-mainnet

Submitting verification for [src/Counter.sol:Counter] 0x8fEc29BdEd7A618ab6E3CD945456A79163995769.
Submitted contract for verification:
        Response: `OK`
        GUID: `fhxxx4wsub68jce24ejvhe68fqabgtpmpzheqpdqvencgph1za`
        URL: https://monadscan.com/address/0x8fec29bded7a618ab6e3cd945456a79163995769
Contract verification status:
Response: `NOTOK`
Details: `Pending in queue`
Warning: Verification is still pending...; waiting 15 seconds before trying again (7 tries remaining)
Contract verification status:
Response: `OK`
Details: `Pass - Verified`
Contract successfully verified
```

Now check the contract on Monadscan.

**Default Foundry Project**

## 1. Update `foundry.toml` with Monad Configuration

```toml lines title="foundry.toml" theme={null}
[profile.default]
src = "src"
out = "out"
libs = ["lib"]
metadata = true
metadata_hash = "none"  # disable ipfs
use_literal_content = true # use source code

# Monad Configuration
eth-rpc-url="https://rpc.monad.xyz"
chain_id = 143
```

## 2. Verify the contract using one of the following block explorers:

**MonadVision**

> [!NOTE]
>
> If you are using MonadVision, you can use
> [this guide](https://docs.blockvision.org/reference/verify-smart-contract-on-monad-explorer#/).
> In particular, the [Verify Contract](https://monadvision.com/verify-contract)
> page provides a convenient way to verify your contract.

```sh theme={null}
forge verify-contract \
    <contract_address> \
    <contract_name> \
    --chain 143 \
    --verifier sourcify \
    --verifier-url https://sourcify-api-monad.blockvision.org/
```

lifecycleEvidence.excerpt: Your all-in-one DeFi Terminal. Swap, trade, earn, launch & more. Swap now links https://app.atlantisdex.xyz/swap/v4; Atlantis V4 modular DEX infrastructure and current pools/earn offerings.
Atlantis has officially deployed its V4 DEX and DeFi Hub on Monad mainnet. Public integration table names the exact Swap Router.

sourceSemantics.deployment: Direct immutable-periphery SwapRouter, not the separately listed position-descriptor proxy. BlockVision runtimeMatch/creationMatch are match, not exact_match.
sourceSemantics.poolTargets: PoolAddress sorts token addresses and CREATE2 derives pool with immutable poolDeployer and POOL_INIT_CODE_HASH 0x62441ebe4e4315cf3d49d5957f94d66b253dbabe7006f34ad7f70947e60bf15c. Nonzero deployer only changes salt to abi.encode(deployer,token0,token1); no arbitrary call target or opaque call payload. CallbackValidation recomputes caller address.
sourceSemantics.bytesLanguage: All outer path bytes interpreted only as alternating token/deployer addresses. No selectors, arbitrary calldata, commands or executor. Source permits unused short trailing suffixes; exactInput path slices 60-byte first pool then advances40 bytes; exactOutput recursion reverses direction.
sourceSemantics.authorityAndUnits: Caller pays tokens via allowance, native MON can wrap to WMON, multihop intermediate router is payer; specified recipient receives final tokens. Token units and WMON use actual token decimals; no dollar-denominated or automatic validation assumption.
sourceSemantics.feesAndConditions: Caller min-output/max-input, sqrt limit and deadline apply as in source. Dynamic Algebra pool/plugin behavior and token tax may affect outcomes. No live pool configuration asserted.
valueAndSettlement: Tokens, amounts, recipient, pool key/deployer, slippage and deadline are caller financial parameters. ERC20 inputs require allowance to this router. A nonzero intended recipient should be used: zero sends output to the router. No withdrawal/sweep/unwrap/refund helper or multicall is admitted, so these standalone swaps do not provide atomic native-output unwrapping or safe recovery of residual native value.

Payment uses router native balance first when input is WMON and balance covers the callback; otherwise it pulls ERC20 from the payer. Overpayment and partial-fill native-input swaps can strand value; residual balance is publicly refundable by excluded helper. Prefer WMON ERC20 input with zero native value for standalone calls; do not send unrelated value.

selectedFunctions.label: Atlantis swap exact input
warnings: Static deployment-bound source and ABI inventory only; not a fresh runtime identity, configuration, balance, liquidity, funding, successful-execution or financial-safety guarantee. Exact grants, canonical calldata/value checks, pauses and all independent execution controls remain mandatory.

Chain143 is Monad mainnet. Direct SwapRouter (not a proxy); verified constructor binds factory 0x10253594a832f967994b44f33411940533302acb, poolDeployer 0xd7cb0e0692f2d55a17ba81c1fe5501d66774fc4a and WNativeToken/WMON 0x3bd359c1119da7da1d913d1c4d2b7c461115433a. ETH-like payable value means native MON, not ETH.

Tokens, amounts, recipient, pool key/deployer, slippage and deadline are caller financial parameters. ERC20 inputs require allowance to this router. A nonzero intended recipient should be used: zero sends output to the router. No withdrawal/sweep/unwrap/refund helper or multicall is admitted, so these standalone swaps do not provide atomic native-output unwrapping or safe recovery of residual native value.

Payment uses router native balance first when input is WMON and balance covers the callback; otherwise it pulls ERC20 from the payer. Overpayment and partial-fill native-input swaps can strand value; residual balance is publicly refundable by excluded helper. Prefer WMON ERC20 input with zero native value for standalone calls; do not send unrelated value.

Path bytes are tokenA(20 bytes), custom deployer(20 bytes), tokenB(20 bytes), repeating deployer+token segments. Exact output reverses the path. Deployer is a financial pool-key salt component, not a call target: targets are CREATE2-derived under immutable poolDeployer and deployed init-code hash; callbacks verify that derivation. Source does not enforce exact path length, and trailing bytes may be ignored; no custom payload/aggregator execution is admitted.

Pool/plugin fees, liquidity and token transfer behavior determine outcomes. The fee-on-transfer variant calls swapWithPaymentInAdvance and compares pool-reported output, not necessarily recipient net taxed-token receipts. A nonzero exact-output single price limit permits less than requested output; source requires full output only with limitSqrtPrice zero.
